solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Former student taken aback by announcement of Scandinavian scientist

indicators.note: taken aback suggests something knocked backwards, so the letters for former student are read in reverse

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out loud, so the word for a Scandinavian is given by its sound

parts.note: a Finn is a native of Finland, often grouped with the Scandinavians

explanation.surface: A one-time pupil is startled by a Nordic researcher being announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' is the reversal signal and 'announcement of' the sound signal; Finns are often loosely counted as Scandinavians.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert, especially a research one.

clue.text: City boss unveiled a mounted assault weapon

indicators.note: unveiled means with its covering, the outer letters, taken away
in a down answer, mounted means raised up, so the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: an AK is a Kalashnikov assault rifle, as in AK-47

explanation.surface: A crime boss reveals a mounted rifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unveiled' strips BOSS to OS; 'mounted' turns AK upwards to KA.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a large port city in Japan, its third most populous.

clue.text: Confused FBI agent accepts erroneous result

indicators.note: one word accepting another takes it inside

parts.note: a fed is a US federal agent, especially of the FBI

indicators.note: erroneous means wrong, so the letters of result are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A rattled federal agent admits an inaccurate finding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erroneous' is the anagram signal; LUSTER is the American spelling, fitting the FBI theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Flustered means agitated and muddled, thrown into a state of nervous confusion.

clue.text: Manipulated reports as required

indicators.note: reports are things heard, so the word for manipulated is given by its sound

parts.note: kneaded means worked or manipulated with the hands, as dough is

explanation.surface: Reports were doctored as the occasion demanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manipulated' suggests tampering, but it is dough being worked: KNEADED, which 'reports' turns into its sound twin.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed and required both mean necessary, wanted for a purpose.

clue.text: Flipping bad smell? Fish stew's contents out of date

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way, so the letters for bad smell run backwards

parts.note: BO is body odour
the sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters, with the outer ones dropped

explanation.surface: A cook grumbles that a stinking fish stew has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reverses BO to OB; 'contents' takes TE from the middle of STEW. 'Flipping' reads as a mild oath, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete is no longer in use, outmoded and superseded by newer things.

clue.text: Plump babe shoots drunk in gripping adaptation

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling about and ending up in a new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of a plump young woman photographed while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges PLUMP BABE SHOOTS; 'gripping' looks like 'thrilling', but it means grasping.
explanation.definitionFit: The thumb that can be pressed against the fingers is an evolutionary adaptation that lets primates grasp things.

clue.text: Famous Greek cardinal makes speech about head of church

parts.note: S is south, one of the four cardinal points of the compass

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: orates means speaks formally, delivers a speech

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Catholic cardinal preaches on the leader of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is a compass point, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the Athenian philosopher of the fifth century BC, one of the best-known ancient Greeks.

clue.text: Haughty socialist embraces love having dropped ecstasy

indicators.note: having dropped something means it is let go, so that letter is removed
one word embracing another holds it inside

parts.note: a lefty is a left-winger, a socialist
love is zero in tennis, written O
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A proud left-winger finds love after giving up drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' puts O inside LEFTY for LEOFTY, and 'having dropped' then takes out E.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty means proud and superior in manner, looking down on others.

clue.text: Witness part-time soldiers fording river

indicators.note: soldiers fording a river are in the middle of it, so their letters sit inside

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England
the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer force
men is a word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Someone watches reservists wading across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a famous trout river in southern England; the TA was Britain's reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is evidence or proof of something, a witness to it, as in 'a testament to her skill'.

clue.text: Muck football team about

parts.note: Man U is the usual short name for Manchester United, an English football club
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that a football side is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN U is Manchester United, a Premier League football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Muck is a farming word for dung spread on fields, the same stuff as manure.

clue.text: Dove father caught with one hand

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral one
a fist is a clenched hand

explanation.surface: Dad grabbed a dove with one hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dove' looks like a bird, or a past tense, but here it is a peace campaigner.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a dove favours peace and negotiation, the opposite of a hawk, like someone opposed to war.

clue.text: Hairs found on rug and bedding

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece found on another is written after it

parts.note: a mat is a small rug
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone finds stray hairs on the rug and the bedclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is the padded base of a bed, part of the bedding one sleeps on.

clue.text: A city street is all the same

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York City
way is a word for a road or street, as in Broadway

explanation.surface: Someone observes that in a certain city every street looks identical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all the same' reads as a description of streets but is the definition, meaning nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean nevertheless, in spite of what has just been said.

clue.text: Time to wake up

definitions.meaning: slang for a prison sentence or prison itself, as in doing time
to rouse or begin to move after sleep, as in 'he did not move a muscle'

explanation.surface: A call that it is time to get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' is prison slang here, not the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is old slang for prison, so time in jail; and to stir is to start moving after sleeping.

clue.text: False note undermines top political party

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece undermining another is placed below it

parts.note: to trump is to beat or top
E is a musical note
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A dishonest memo damages a leading party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like an adjective for the party, but it is a verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumped-up charge is invented and fraudulent, so false.

clue.text: Bad vibes holding English boy back in colonies

indicators.note: one set of letters holding another keeps them inside it
bad suggests the letters of vibes are spoilt, put into a new order
back means the word for boy is read in reverse

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a boy

explanation.surface: A boy from England picks up a bad atmosphere and retreats to the settlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' is the anagram signal, 'holding' the insertion and 'back' the reversal; the inserted letters sit just after the first B.
explanation.definitionFit: A beehive houses a colony of bees, so beehives are bee colonies.

clue.text: Setter's politically correct about Eton- schooled earl's inadequacy

parts.note: the setter is I, so setter's is I'm, I am

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the letters of PC go round the other piece
schooled suggests the letters of Eton are trained into a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: The setter calls an Etonian earl's failings correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schooled' is the anagram signal and 'about' the insertion; the stray hyphen in 'Eton- schooled' is just the printed clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Impotence is powerlessness, a lack of the strength or ability to act.

clue.text: Home provided care for fiancée

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'stay in'
tended means looked after, cared for

explanation.surface: A care home looked after someone's bride-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's intended is the woman he is engaged to marry, his betrothed.

clue.text: Festival of dunces dancing around a pole

indicators.note: the anagram goes around the other letters, holding them inside
dancing letters move about and land in a new order

parts.note: N is the north pole

explanation.surface: At a festival, some dimwits dance round a maypole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges DUNCES as SUNDCE, and 'around' puts A and N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundance is the American film festival held each year in Utah, founded by Robert Redford.

clue.text: Some advice about bread

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the phrase for some advice is read backwards

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: Someone offers a few pointers on baking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some advice' looks like a hidden-word signal, but it is A TIP, turned round by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pita is a flat Middle Eastern bread that opens into a pocket.

clue.text: Initially propounded concerns in depressing newspaper article

indicators.note: in places the following pieces inside the word for depressing

parts.note: sad can mean depressing, as in a sad state

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

parts.note: re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A gloomy news piece that first sets out worries.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a feature covering facing pages of a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Helicopter's acceleration rate maintains height

parts.note: a is the symbol for acceleration in physics

indicators.note: one word maintains another by keeping it held within

parts.note: pace means rate or speed

explanation.surface: A technical note that a helicopter keeps its altitude as it speeds up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache is a US Army attack helicopter, named after the Native American people.

clue.text: Soprano's overwhelmed by revolutionary musical

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece overwhelmed by another is under it, written after

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine-born Marxist revolutionary
S is soprano, and soprano's taken as S's, the plural of the letter, gives two of them

explanation.surface: An opera singer is swamped by a rebel musical production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Che' is the usual crossword revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a 1980s stage show with music by Benny and Björn of ABBA, set in a Cold War tournament.

clue.text: He strips off for fashionistas

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man undresses for a crowd of style-conscious onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the letters of HE STRIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hipsters are trendy people who follow alternative fashions closely, like fashionistas.

clue.text: Run over military police officer's missing daughter

indicators.note: missing means going without, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a redcap is a British military policeman, named for his red cap cover

explanation.surface: A military policeman knocked down, with his daughter absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run over' suggests a car accident, but it means go through again.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to recapitulate, going back over the main points again briefly.

clue.text: Present study by retired doctor about universal supplement

parts.note: AD, the era we live in now, stands for the present time
a den is a private study

indicators.note: about means wrapped around, so one piece sits inside the other
retired means drawn back, so the letters for doctor are read in reverse

parts.note: MD is a Doctor of Medicine
U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A gift of research, by a retired medic, about a universal remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns MD into DM, and 'about' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is something added at the end of a book or document, an appendix or extra section.

clue.text: Harem guard from Europe roughly abducted by retreating barbarian

parts.note: EU is the European Union

indicators.note: being abducted by someone means being held inside them
retreating means going backwards, so the barbarian's letters are reversed

parts.note: a Hun was one of the barbarian invaders of the Roman Empire
c is circa, meaning roughly or about

explanation.surface: A tale of a harem's protector seized by a fleeing barbarian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns HUN to NUH, and 'abducted by' places C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrated men served as guards and attendants in the harems of Ottoman and other courts.

clue.text: Records broken by international poetry events

indicators.note: a word broken by another is split open with the other inside

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: Global poetry readings are disrupting record releases.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is an incident or a single event in a series, such as a stage in someone's life.

clue.text: Pass by protective gear in port

parts.note: to pass away is to die
PPE is personal protective equipment

explanation.surface: Instructions to walk past the safety equipment at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just links the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a French ferry port on the English Channel coast of Normandy.
